book_title: Prologue: The Business, The Price & Our Independent Verdict
question: What does Mondelēz International do, and why do we downgrade MDLZ to REJECTED (TIER_0, VALUATION) despite a Q3 2026 operational inflection?

epigraph.quote: A great consumer franchise at an uncompelling risk-reward price is still a pass; protecting dry powder in a Downtrend beats stretching for 1.01-to-1 odds.
epigraph.author: Mondelez Underwriting Synthesis

web_blocks.html: What Mondelēz Does: Mondelēz International (NASDAQ: MDLZ) is a global pure-play snacking leader. It generated $38.54 billion in FY2025 revenue across 150+ countries [4, 10]. Biscuits & Baked Snacks account for 47.7% of sales (Oreo, Ritz, LU, Clif Bar), while Chocolate adds 32.9% (Cadbury, Milka, Toblerone) and Gum & Candy adds 10.5% [4, 20]. Roughly 40% of revenue comes from emerging markets, including 5 million+ outlets in India and 1 million+ stores in Brazil [12, 28].

Independent Dual Verdict: Pass 1 awarded MDLZ a price-blind COMPOUNDER_PASS (PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health). Pass 2 downgrades MDLZ to REJECTED (TIER_0, reason: VALUATION) at CMP $66.28 (2026-11-20; $66.08 on 2026-11-23 snapshot). Probability-weighting Bear $54.00 (25%), Base $71.00 (55%), and Bull $82.00 (20%) yields a $68.95 Expected Value (+4.0%), leaving only 0.89:1–1.01:1 R:R against our $61.61 stop. Our positions ledger confirms MDLZ is NOT_HELD (0 shares), and we retain 100% Treasury Cash.

web_blocks.html: Bull vs. Bear in One Minute: Bulls point to Q3 2026's inflection: volume/mix rose +1.8 pp, adjusted gross margin expanded +380 bps YoY to 34.2%, and ~65% of revenue held or gained share [12, 23, 42]. Bears highlight Q3 balance-sheet strain (CP +38.1% to $3,610M, $20,115M Net Debt, $1,212M AR drag, -$245M derivative cash outflow, $64M impairments, USMCA tariff exclusion, CEO 258,570-share sale) and Red Team's $68.25 ($3.25 EPS) / $53.63 (-19.1%) stress math [29, 42, 44, 45]. Our view: respect the business, reject the valuation.

book_paragraphs: Every time you walk past a supermarket end-cap stacked with Oreo cookies, Ritz crackers, or Cadbury Dairy Milk bars, you are looking at one of the most resilient distribution machines in global consumer packaged goods. Mondelēz International generates $38.54 billion in annual revenue across more than 150 countries, with roughly 40% of sales rooted in emerging markets—including over 5 million retail outlets in India and 1 million stores in Brazil.

In Q3 2026, Mondelēz turned an operational corner as cocoa entered a 500,000-ton surplus: volume and mix inflected to +1.8 percentage points and adjusted gross margin expanded 380 basis points year-over-year to 34.2%. On a strictly price-blind basis, Chapters 1 through 6 award Mondelēz a COMPOUNDER_PASS business quality verdict.

Yet great underwriting refuses to stretch for an uncompelling price. Probability-weighting Bear $54.00 (25%), Base $71.00 (55%), and Bull $82.00 (20%) yields an Expected Value of $68.95, leaving only 0.89-to-1 to 1.01-to-1 reward-to-risk at $66.28 against our $61.61 stop. Red Team stress-testing proved that at $3.25 FY2027E EPS, even a 21.0x multiple yields $68.25—failing our 1.50-to-1 hurdle even on a pullback to $64.50—while a 16.5x bear multiple implies $53.63 (-19.1%).

Combined with Q3 2026 balance-sheet creep (commercial paper up 38.1% to $3,610 million, $20,115 million Net Debt, $1,212 million AR drag, -$245 million derivative cash outflow, $64 million biscuit impairments, USMCA tariff exclusion, and CEO Dirk Van de Put's 258,570-share sale) inside a 38.8%-breadth US Downtrend, we downgrade MDLZ to REJECTED (TIER_0, VALUATION), confirm NOT_HELD (0 shares), decline the 2027-01-15 $70/$77.5 call spread, and keep 100% in Treasury cash.
As you listen through the chapters ahead, keep one rule in mind: we separate business quality from stock price so we never fall in love with a brand at the wrong valuation.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: How to Read This 10-Chapter Monograph
book_callouts.quote: Chapters 1 through 6 prove Mondelēz is a COMPOUNDER_PASS business; Chapters 7 through 9 prove why $66.28—and even $64.50—earns a clean REJECTED.
book_callouts.text: Separating business quality from entry asymmetry lets us admire Oreo and Cadbury while refusing 0.89:1–1.01:1 odds and debt-funded buybacks.
